key_insight: Linear stochastic optimization of PV-battery control can cut equivalent carbon emissions far more effectively than heuristic rule-based charging, approaching an omniscient lower bound.
engineering_relevance: The work shows that tractable linear programs can support emission-aware battery dispatch in residential solar storage systems under uncertain load, generation, and grid carbon intensity.
method: Built a hierarchy from self-consumption heuristics to stochastic programs with linear feedback control
Modeled uncertainty using large scenario sets derived from principal component analysis of real operational data
Compared anticipative and feedback-based formulations against an omniscient benchmark
evidence_signal: Synthetic yet realistic experiments show the programmed battery model substantially outperforms heuristics and comes close to the theoretical lower bound, while feedback models add compute cost without improving unseen-data performance.
watch_item: Results depend on scenario quality and may not generalize if real household demand, PV output, or grid-carbon patterns differ from the training data.
paper_title: Comparative Analysis of Linear Battery Models for Carbon Emission Optimization in Solar Energy Systems
